claim: On 2025-09-16 AWS Storage Gateway announced IPv6 support for its endpoints, APIs and gateway appliance interfaces, with new dual-stack endpoints that give both IPv6 and IPv4 access.
question: Does Storage Gateway support IPv6, and since when?

qualifiers.scope: Storage Gateway endpoints, APIs and appliance interfaces
qualifiers.condition: the existing IPv4-only endpoints remain available

evidence.quote: AWS Storage Gateway announces Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) support for AWS Storage Gateway endpoints, APIs, and gateway appliance interfaces. This enhancement enables both IPv6 and IPv4 access to our new dual-stack endpoints.

evidence.heading: AWS Storage Gateway now supports IPv6

note: d25-044. Examinable, recent. Older questions assume IPv4 only.

claim: On 2025-09-30 AWS Storage Gateway added support for VPC endpoint policies, so administrators can attach endpoint policies to VPC endpoints for granular access control over Storage Gateway direct APIs.
question: Can you attach an endpoint policy to a VPC endpoint for Storage Gateway, and since when?

evidence.quote: AWS Storage Gateway now supports Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) endpoint policies for your VPC endpoints. With this feature, administrators can attach endpoint policies to VPC endpoints, allowing granular access control over Storage Gateway direct APIs for improved data protection and security posture.

evidence.heading: AWS Storage Gateway now supports VPC endpoint policies

claim: On 2025-12-22 AWS Storage Gateway added the Nutanix AHV hypervisor as a deployment option for S3 File, Tape and Volume gateways.
question: Can Storage Gateway be deployed on the Nutanix AHV hypervisor, and since when?

qualifiers.scope: gateway deployment options for S3 File, Tape and Volume gateways

evidence.quote: The AWS Storage Gateway service now supports the Nutanix AHV hypervisor as a deployment option for S3 File, Tape and Volume gateways.

evidence.heading: AWS Storage Gateway now supports Nutanix AHV hypervisor
